cohort: The study included 67 patients from two tertiary centers, consisting of 32 controls, 12 with placenta previa, and 23 with placenta accreta.
finding: Maternal Elabela levels were significantly different across control, placenta previa, and accreta groups, with specific cut-off values demonstrating potential as a biochemical predictor for placenta previa (sensitivity 83.3%, specificity 83.6%) and placenta accreta (sensitivity 60.9%, specificity 61.4%).
